answers.years_customer_support: My customer-facing experience comes from roles that required the same core skills as a formal support position, even when the job title wasn't 'Customer Support': • Binary Options Product Review (2016–2018, ~2 years): live chat and Skype onboarding/support for ~200–300 users, helping them understand and use a financial platform. I exceeded monthly conversion targets set by my manager and earned performance bonuses. • Advanced Elite PC Solutions, Nerja, Spain (2011–2012, ~1 year): IT apprentice at the counter — diagnosing issues, selling hardware, and acting as English↔Spanish interpreter/translator for international customers. • Several years in hospitality (restaurants): direct customer service, problem-solving under pressure, clear communication. • Crypto communities (2018–present): regularly helping users in Telegram and Discord with onboarding, wallet setup, transactions and security — I'd estimate meaningful guidance and Q&A for users over the last ~5 years, not full-time. In total: ~3 years of direct professional customer-facing work plus 5+ years of community user education.
answers.crypto_experience: 7+ years of continuous, self-directed hands-on exposure to crypto and blockchain (2018–present): self-custody, hardware wallets, exchanges (Binance, Kraken, KuCoin, Bitget), DEXs (SundaeSwap, Minswap, PancakeSwap), DeFi, staking, tokenomics research, whitepaper translation and community support. My knowledge is both practical and theoretical: I use these tools daily for personal investing, and I've regularly helped friends, family and community members as an independent informal consultant — guiding them through wallet setup, transactions, gas-fee issues, network selection, security best practices, and general crypto concepts. I'm an active participant in several Telegram communities (and occasionally Discord), where I help users troubleshoot and learn. I'm a true believer in the crypto/blockchain philosophy and I stay continuously up to date with the ecosystem.
